The government has approved the establishment of a new medical college at the Sarangpur campus of the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh. The project will be developed with an investment of Rs 456 crore and is expected to offer an annual intake of 125 MBBS students.Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda announced the approval through a social media post. He said the project would strengthen medical education infrastructure and contribute to the development of a skilled healthcare workforce in the country. The proposed institution will come up across nearly 51 acres at the Sarangpur campus.

Advt

New medical college to have modern training facilitiesAccording to the minister, the proposed medical college will be equipped with modern laboratories, advanced simulation facilities, clinical training infrastructure and research facilities.The infrastructure is planned to support medical education and practical training, allowing students to gain exposure to clinical practices alongside their academic studies. With an annual intake capacity of 125 MBBS students, the institution will add to the country's medical education capacity.

The project is also expected to strengthen PGIMER's presence in Chandigarh by expanding its educational infrastructure at the Sarangpur campus.

Project aligned with Centre's medical education expansion plansNadda said the approval represents another step towards fulfilling Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of adding 75,000 medical seats across the country over the next five years.

The Centre has been focusing on expanding medical education infrastructure and increasing the availability of trained healthcare professionals. The proposed college is part of this broader effort to improve access to medical education and strengthen the healthcare workforce.The addition of 125 MBBS seats annually will contribute to the country's undergraduate medical education capacity. The proposed laboratories, simulation facilities and research infrastructure are intended to support students' academic learning and clinical skill development.

Advt

The government has approved the project with a proposed investment of Rs 456 crore. Further details regarding construction timelines, admission commencement and the first batch of students have not been specified in the announcement.
